messages:
alex: Heads-up — support ticket: multiple orgs got immediate 429s this morning even though our metering pipeline shows usage still under committed quota. /cc @mira @jonathan

mira: Saw that. Initial suspicion: metering ingestion laged ~30-90s from our batch aggregators, but enforcement uses the realtime shard counters that are updated from API gateway. mismatch possible when bursts + delayed reconciliation.

jonathan: Quick summary of why this happens: enforcement uses a token-bucket implementation fed by the realtime request stream, but the dashboard and billing rely on the metering pipeline (kinesis -> batch processor -> clickhouse) which is eventually consistent. When the batch lags, users see 'we used less' but enforcement already consumed tokens.

alex: Right — customers see console showing remaining quota that differs from what they actually hit. They get surprised when enforcement denies requests while dashboard says they have credit. bad UX.

sara: We need a short-term mitigation and a long-term fix. Short: make enforcement more forgiving for small bursts (grace tokens or soft-429 with warning) and surface a clear console banner: "Enforcement may lag reconciliation by N seconds".

mira: Agreed. Also: add a new telemetry metric: enforcement_denies_vs_metered_diff per-org per-minute. That will let us alert on the diff spike instead of waiting for support tickets.

jonathan: Proposed technical options — pick one asap: 
1) Keep token-bucket but backfill it from an append-only real-time increments stream (kinesis) so both enforcement and metering read same source. Requires low-latency consumer for the bucket (ops work).
2) Hedge enforcement: check primary realtime bucket, but if bucket empty and metered_recent_window > 0 then allow a small grace (X tokens) and emit a reconciliation event to possibly revoke/credit later.
3) Switch enforcement to only use the realtime counter with leaky-bucket smoothing and always surface 'soft' limit for 1-2 minutes after a spike.

alex: I like 2) for fast rollout. Implement via a feature flag so we can flip without deploy. Also add immediate billing refund path if reconciliation later says they were under quota.

sara: For UI/ops: need a toggle in Console -> Quotas: "Enable enforcement hedging (soft grace)" with description and rollback. I can add copy. Also add a per-org indicator that shows when hedging is active.

mira: Implementation sketch for 2) — pseudo: 

```lua
-- redis lua for atomic check+hedge
local key = KEYS[1] -- token bucket key
local now = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local tokens = tonumber(redis.call('GET', key) or '0')
local metered_recent = tonumber(redis.call('GET', key .. ':recent') or '0')
local grace = tonumber(ARGV[2]) -- e.g. 50 tokens
if tokens > 0 then
  redis.call('DECRBY', key, 1)
  return {true, 'enforced'}
end
if metered_recent > 0 and metered_recent <= grace * 10 then
  -- allow short soft-grant and emit a reconciliation message
  redis.call('INCRBY', key .. ':soft', 1)
  return {true, 'soft-granted'}
end
return {false, 'deny'}
```

jonathan: Important: when soft-granted, we MUST emit an event (topic: enforcement.soft_grant) with org, request_id, timestamp so metering/billing can reconcile and charge/credit later. Also mark request logs so customer support can filter.

alex: Ops notes: set default grace to very small (10-50 tokens) and set notification threshold (if >0.5% of requests for an org are soft-granted in a 5m window, auto-disable hedging for that org and page oncall). We don't want unchecked overuse.

sara: I'll add console UX for per-org overrides and the auto-disable notice. Also will add a short FAQ entry and billing note that we might issue credits on reconciliation.

mira: For the longer term, we should converge enforcement and metering onto the same real-time stream so both have a single source of truth. Plan: realtime ingestion -> small stateful consumer that maintains bucket counters (redis) + writes events to metering topic for billing. Then batch/analytics will read from the same events for accuracy.

jonathan: Roadmap: short-term (48h): feature flag + redis lua hedging + telemetry + console toggle + support doc. Medium (2-6w): build real-time counter consumer and migrate enforcement to it, deprecate dual pipelines.

alex: Action items: 
- sara: console toggle + FAQ + banner (PR today)
- jonathan: implement redis lua + event emission + feature-flag kill-switch (PR w/ tests in 24h)
- mira: add telemetry metric & dashboard + pager rule (alert on diff spike)
- alex: notify sales/support + drafted customer email template for affected orgs

sara: Filed draft PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pull/437 (WIP) — adding toggle and banner copy.

jonathan: I'll open infra PR for the lua and feature-flag: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/992. Planning canary on staging -> 10% prod -> 50% prod over 48h.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1173 (quota-enforcement-lag). Pager duty: oncall-eng.

alex: Thanks everyone — let's sync in 2h to review telemetry data and decide on default flag state.

mira: +1. I'll have the dashboard ready by then.

sara: Will update the PR and console mockups in the next 90m.

jonathan: Starting work now, will push a test build to staging and ping this thread when ready.

alex: Great. pinged @support with a customer-facing note and provisional credits process.

sara: small UX note: add explicit "last reconciled at" timestamp next to the quota number in console so customers stop assuming realtime parity.

jonathan: +1 on that. will add a call in the quota API response header: X-Quota-Last-Reconciled

alex: closing loop. follow-ups in this thread. thanks!
